content:
You may hear that your GP has recorded you as frail. This can feel worrying, but it can open the door to extra support.

This guide explains what it can mean. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

How frailty is identified

Practices may use tools such as the electronic frailty index, alongside clinical judgement. Arrangements differ across the UK.

What it can lead to

  • A medicine review.
  • Falls risk assessment.
  • Care planning.
  • Referral to other services.

Questions to ask

  • What does this mean for me?
  • Can I have a medicine review?
  • Who can help with strength and balance?

Frailty can change

Frailty can sometimes improve with activity, nutrition and support.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can I see what is recorded?

You can ask your practice.

Will it affect my treatment?

It should help tailor care, not reduce it.

Sources and further reading

  • British Geriatrics Society: Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment toolkit
  • Rockwood K et al. A global clinical measure of fitness and frailty in elderly people. CMAJ 2005
  • NHS: Medicines reviews and polypharmacy (NICE NG5: Medicines optimisation)

Educational information for people in the United Kingdom — not a diagnosis or personal medical advice. Charity no. 1218461. Reviewed by Louis Maxwell (HCPC PH128483). Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
